question: How is the model transferred to other languages?

answer.free_form_answer: Build a bilingual language model,   learn the target language specific parameters starting from a pretrained English LM , fine-tune both English and target model to obtain the bilingual LM.
evidence: Do multilingual models always need to be trained from scratch? Can we transfer linguistic knowledge learned by English pre-trained models to other languages? In this work, we develop a technique to rapidly transfer an existing pre-trained model from English to other languages in an energy efficient way BIBREF8. As the first step, we focus on building a bilingual language model (LM) of English and a target language. Starting from a pre-trained English LM, we learn the target language specific parameters (i.e., word embeddings), while keeping the encoder layers of the pre-trained English LM fixed. We then fine-tune both English and target model to obtain the bilingual LM. We apply our approach to autoencoding language models with masked language model objective and show the advantage of the proposed approach in zero-shot transfer. title: From English To Foreign Languages: Transferring Pre-trained Language Models
answer_short: By transferring an existing pre-trained model from English to other languages under a limited computational budget, keeping encoder layers fixed and fine-tuning target language specific parameters.
answer_rationale: The model is transferred by starting from a pre-trained English LM, learning target language specific parameters (e.g., word embeddings) while keeping the encoder layers fixed, and then fine-tuning both English and target model to obtain a bilingual LM. This approach is energy-efficient and can be done with a single GPU, as described in Text 2 and Text 6.
